fixture.declaredMethod: Convex hull (monotone chain) in EPSG:32630. Encloses 139230.0 m² across 498 m at its widest. A hull far longer than it is wide is a line the projection did not quite flatten, and should be read as one. A hull is convex. A distribution that is not — cases along a river, facilities along a coast — is filled in, so the hull asserts area where nothing was observed. It is an outline of what was observed, not a service area, a catchment or a boundary anyone agreed to.

criterion: the same number of hull vertices, every vertex within 0.001 m of one in the reference hull and vice versa, planar area within 0.05 m2, span within 0.1 m, and the located-point count unchanged
notEstablished: That a convex hull is a sensible summary of these deaths. It is convex, so it fills in ground the outbreak did not cross and asserts area where nothing was observed. Both implementations assert it identically.
